text.p: Dutch publisher De Telegraaf said on Sunday it was maintaining its full-year 1996 profit forecast following the collapse of TV channel Sport7, in which it holds a five percent stake.

"The application for court protection from creditors -- leading to liquidation -- of Sport 7...will in the first instance have no substantial effect on the company's profit outlook for 1996," De Telegraaf said in a statement.
De Telegraaf said it was making no provisions for its share in a 180 million guilder bank guarantee extended by Sport7's shareholders to Dutch football association KNVB.
"The claim on the...bank guarantee is disputed; for this reason De Telegraaf will not make a provision at this stage," it said, adding it bore a maximum net risk of 6.5 million guilders.

The bank guarantee was aimed at covering KNVB's risk in the event it might be forced to re-sell the broadcasting rights for Dutch first division matches for less than the seven-year 1.04 billion guilder deal clinched with Sport7.
De Telegraaf reiterated its August forecast of significantly lower 1996 profits than the 101.3 million guilders of 1995.
It said earnings had been pressured by start-up costs of its shares in commercial television stations.
Apart from its stake in Sport7, De Telegraaf also holds a 30 percent stake in commercial channel SBS6.
